evidence: Scope: every criterion in 2 gates + functional (36) + polish (5) + visual (5 likert). Most criteria are concrete, browser-observable and durable: shared state is read back in an independent context (constraints gate, hro_arrive_bottom, hro_reorder, hro_bulk_move, hro_undo_restores, hro_job_open), refusals require a positive control plus before/after facts and server replays with a fresh version (functional prompt.md:13,17,27,31), restart re-reads many revisions including seeded order/note recorded in Z (hro_restart; prompt.md:33,59), probes are distinctive and absent from the seed (per-review suffixed names; 'plain', 'Call back on Fri' and 'distinctive reply' texts not in seed_data.json; seeded facts checked: Platform Engineer Applied Greta/Ade/Marco, Screen Priya/Samuel, Noor note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.', Lena read_count 2 of 3 with the third message by USR-REC3 => 1 unread, Noor long thread 120 messages, page size 30). Lesson 14/7 (timing void/repeat handling) is satisfied for every positive 'within 15 seconds' step: functional prompt.md:21 and polish prompt.md:18 define one browser_run_code_unsafe action, t0 after a successful trigger, 500 ms polling, void definition, at most two repeats, fail if all void; visual and gates have no timed steps. Lesson 9 (report every step) is present in functional:25, polish:22, visual:18. Lesson 13: only localhost addresses. Suites run sequentially (test.sh:207 '--max-concurrent-agent 1'). DEFECT 1 (Fail, P2) — negative 'still not seen' leg in hro_seen has no decidable observation window or durable readback. functional judge.toml:364 'after only the Observer opens the conversation it is still not seen'; protocol U (prompt.md:49) 'Aud opens the conversation: still not seen; Tomas opens it: seen' and 'Every reading in U that follows another person's action is a timed observation'. The timed-observation procedure (prompt.md:21) polls 'until the expected change is present'; for a negative expectation the expected state ('not seen') is already present at t0, so the reading is met at ~0 ms, before any live update (SSE/poll) could carry a wrongly-set seen mark to Rafael's page. Nothing requires waiting the full 15 s, reloading Rafael's page, or reading in a fresh Rafael context before Tomas opens. The probe therefore leaves no trace that distinguishes the defect it exists to catch (rules hireops_rules.md:171 'The observer opening a conversation never counts'). Same pattern, weaker instances (Note-level, included for 'every instance'): hro_unread_counts judge.toml:346 'while it is open at its newest message Tomas's next message does not raise his count or total' is read at the moment the message appears, so an app that raises the count via a slower channel after the message renders would pass; hro_unread_scrolled_up judge.toml:355 'stays unread until he goes to it' is read when the notice appears, with no instruction to confirm the unread state persists (and no stated place to read it if the layout hides the conversation list while a conversation is open). DEFECT 2 (risk, part of this Fail) — hro_refused_put_back (judge.toml:139, weight 2) is not decidable when a conforming UI does not offer the over-capacity move. Protocol L (prompt.md:39) tries Screen->Interview on a full Interview 'through the UI', while prompt.md:31 states 'Whether a refused action is offered at all is the app's choice' and directs a replay when not offered. If the app disables or hides the Interview move because it can already see Interview is full, the page shows no refusal reason and no rollback, and the criterion's only alternative pass path ('A UI that refuses before the card moves, with the reason shown and focus on that card') may or may not cover a disabled control with no message. Judges will split on the same conforming app, and an app that never implements optimistic rollback can be indistinguishable from one that does. Golden evidence: raw-evidence-index scripted golden run (hashes verified) is not a configured judge run; it does not exercise either defect, and no Oracle, model or portal score exists. Defect 1 is a false-pass (weak probe) risk; Defect 2 is a conforming-alternative false-fail and decidability risk.
counterexample: Broken app for Defect 1: computes 'seen' for a staff message as 'opened by anyone other than the sender' (so the Observer counts) and refreshes the sender's view by a 5-10 s poll (or even ~300 ms SSE debounce as the golden uses). Judge: Aud opens the conversation in an independent context; the timed reading of Rafael's page sees 'Sent/not seen' at t0 (expected state already present, met=true at ~0 ms); Tomas then opens and 'Seen' appears within 15 s; Bill/Rafael legs pass normally. hro_seen (weight 1.5) passes despite violating 'The observer opening a conversation never counts'. Conforming alternative for Defect 2: an app that rolls back optimistic moves on any server refusal (e.g. 409 stale) but disables the Interview move button with a tooltip when the board already shows Interview full; protocol L finds the move not offered, the replay is refused (hro_interview_full passes), but no on-page reason/rollback/focus is observable, so hro_refused_put_back (weight 2) can be scored 0 or 1 depending on the judge's reading.
suggested_fix: In protocol U, after only the Observer opens the conversation, require a durable negative read: wait the full 15 s timed window confirming Rafael's message is never shown as seen, then reload Rafael's page (or read in a fresh Rafael context) and confirm it is still not seen before Tomas opens it (apply the same 'hold for the window, then reload-confirm' rule to the 'count does not rise' and 'stays unread' legs); and in hro_refused_put_back state explicitly how a not-offered over-capacity move is scored (e.g. a disabled/hidden move with a visible capacity reason on that card passes) or provoke a refusal the client cannot foresee.
